#!/bin/sh
# Session 9 (2026-11-09): the learner (a warehouse picker) reviewed the realistic-freight build: the layers are still too
# perfect. On real orders you often can't finish a layer level: you build a one-sided step (a "hill") for a while and
# fix it further down the order, or add to the other side. Add one such stepped layer, re-test, re-record.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." || exit 1
claude -p "$(cat <<'PROMPT'
Lens Studio is open with this project (Stack Right; devpost/design-brief.md is the approved brief). Work through the CLAD skills and the Lens Studio MCP. Bash and ffmpeg (C:/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg.exe) are available. Read Assets/Scripts/*.ts first; StackRightPickList.ts owns the order and the computed plan. devpost/agent-logs/run_shapes_v6.sh and 08-shapes-v6.jsonl show the last session (how it built, tested and recorded).

The learner (who picks real store orders) says the layers are still too perfect: on a real order you often can't finish a layer level, so you build a one-sided step (a hill) for a while, then fix it down the line or add to the other side. Teach exactly that in layer 4. Keep every existing rule, interaction, the ghost/tag/snap/tip/card behaviour, shapes, the pallet jack, the demo driver and the tests working.

1. Order change (still heaviest first). Insert before the tomato trays, in layer 4:
   SOUP 24x500g, 11 kg, carton, w 38, d 57, h 26, count 3, not fragile, a bright light colour not used yet (e.g. light teal or lilac-pink; additive display, no dark colours).
   Layer 4 becomes: 3 soup cases, then the 6 TINNED TOMATOES 2x24 trays (h 13) that are already there. Totals: 34 cases, top = 84 + 26 = 110 cm for layer 4, 140 cm with layer 5. Layers 1-3 and 5 unchanged.

2. Plan: support a stepped layer, still computed from case sizes, not hand-placed. Add a per-line zone to the order data ("far" = back half, z from -58.25 to 0; "near" = front half, z from 0 to +58.25, near = toward the user; default "full" = the whole pallet as now). In layer 4, soup is "far", tomatoes are "near". Within a zone, row-pack as now but inside the zone's rectangle (rows centred in x, the zone's rows centred in the zone's z range). When the next case does not fit the zone's current tier, start a new tier in that zone on top of it (stack on the tier below; tier = rows). So: soup = 3 across (38 x 57 footprint each, 114 x 57), one tier, back half, 26 high. Tomatoes = 38 x 57 footprints (check the orientation that gives 3 across x 57 deep), 3 per tier in the front half, two tiers of 13 = 26, so the front comes back level with the back. The layer's top is level only when the layer is finished; print an error if a finished layer is not level, if a zone overflows, or if the step between zones ever exceeds one case height (26 cm) during the build.
   Check the joints of layer 4 still cross layer 3 (layer 3 has joints at x = 0 and z = +-19 cm, juice at x = +-29), and layer 5 crosses layer 4. Say so in the report. The tag stays "Layer 4 · K of 34 · kg". The ghost for each tray on the second tier sits on top of the first-tier tray (real snapping height). Placing a tray before the soup is impossible anyway (one case at a time), so no new mistake rule is needed.

3. The teaching moment: when the last soup case lands, show a step note (same style and place as the layer-done note, for about 3.5 s or until the next case is grabbed) with two lines: "Not enough soup for a full layer: step at the back." / "The trays fill the front, two high, back to level." Change the layer 3 done note to be true for what follows (e.g. "Layer 3 done.\nHeavy soup next: back half first.") and layer 4's to "Layer 4 done.\nThe front caught up: level again." Layer 5 done note unchanged. Log "[StackRight] step note" when it shows.

4. Demo driver ("demo" mode in StackRightTestDriver.ts): keep all beat names and their [DEMO] log lines: intro, case1, overhang, gap, case2, layer1, layer2, layer3mixed, fast, layer5, complete, reset, end. "fast" now starts layer 4: soup at 1.2 s per case; then log "[DEMO] hill" and hold 4 s on the step note with the hill in view; then the trays at 0.8 s per case; after the last tray log "[DEMO] level" and hold 1.5 s. "layer5" now goes at 2.2 s per case (still hovering 1.5 s over the ghost for the paper towel). Other timings unchanged. Default driver mode must be "off" when you finish.

5. Tests: update the self-test checks and the LEAF scenarios (Assets/Tests and copies in devpost/leaf-scenarios) for 34 cases, 140 cm, the tags, the per-layer notes, the step note. New checks: layer 4 has two zones; the back is 26 cm higher than the front after the soup (the step), and the step never exceeds 26 cm; the second-tier tray ghosts sit on top of first-tier trays; layer 4 is level when finished; joints cross for every layer; no overlaps between cases in the same zone and tier; everything inside the pallet. Run them; append results to devpost/selftest-2026-11-09.log. Everything must pass.

6. Look at it: CapturePanelScreenshotTool of the Preview at the demo camera at (a) the step note with the hill in view, (b) mid tray second tier, (c) the completion card; save as devpost/screenshots/v5-*.png and check by eye that the step reads as a step, the note is readable and not hidden by the pallet jack or cases, and the card shows 34 cases and 140 cm under/around the 180 cm line legibly. Fix what doesn't.

7. Re-record exactly as last time (see 08-shapes-v6.jsonl for preview size, ffmpeg gdigrab region, camera): 30 fps, x264 crf 18, to devpost/video/raw_demo.mp4 (overwrite; first copy the current one to devpost/video/raw_demo_take5.mp4 and demo_beats.log/record_start.txt to *_take5.*); record_start.txt with ms; all [DEMO] and [StackRight] lines to devpost/video/demo_beats.log in the same format as now; stop ffmpeg with q right after "[DEMO] end". Extract check frames devpost/video/check-hill-note.png (at hill + 2 s), check-level.png (at level + 0.5 s), and refresh check-completion-card.png; look at each. Set the driver back to "off" and save the scene.

Known gotchas: injected mouse input does not register grabs; CaptureRuntimeViewTool and the preview-interaction package install can freeze Lens Studio; open pop-ups silently block the TypeScript compiler (if compiles stop reporting, say so instead of looping). Don't touch .agents/skills, .claude/skills or Plugins/. Units are cm; keep everything bright.

Do not git commit, push, or touch anything outside this project folder. When done, print a short report: what changed per file, the computed plan for layer 4 (zones, tiers, footprints, heights) and whether joints cross for every layer, test totals, recording path/length, demo beat times relative to recording start, what each check frame showed, and anything unfinished or that looks off.

1	// StackRightPickList.ts
2	// STAND-IN FOR BARCODE SCAN. A real picker's Lens would read the case's barcode when it is
3	// picked up. For the preview, the order is fixed: 31 cases of real store freight (sacks, cartons,
4	// shrink-wrapped tin trays, a long carton) in the warehouse system's heaviest-first sequence
5	// (5 layers). The learner should replace these lines with real order lines.
6	//
7	// Owns: the order (case data: name, weight, class, real size in cm, shape, colour, turned flag)
8	// and the LOAD PLAN, which is generated in code from the case sizes (not hand-placed): each layer
9	// is row (shelf) packed - cases in order, left to right while a row fits the 116.5 cm pallet, a
10	// new row nearer the user when it doesn't, row depth = deepest case in it, every row centred in x
11	// and the layer centred in z. Also the plan checks (overlaps, level layers, crossing joints).
12	// Pure data/logic, no scene access.
13	// Must not: touch the scene, hold game state.
14	//
15	// Case sizes are W (x) x H (y) x D (z) in cm, in the case's own frame. Plan positions are in
16	// Pallet-local cm: x right, z toward the user (near edge = +z), y up from the floor.
17	// Pallet deck top is at y = 15.
18	
19	/** How the case is drawn: carton (box), sack (soft bag), tray (tins in a shrink-wrapped tray), long (112 cm carton). */
20	export type CaseShape = "carton" | "sack" | "tray" | "long"
21	
22	export interface CaseSpec {
23	  key: string // used in scene object names, e.g. Case_03_PetFood
24	  name: string // printed on the case
25	  kg: number
26	  fragile: boolean // true = crushable, goes on top
27	  layer: number // 1..5
28	  size: vec3 // W x H x D, cm (case frame)
29	  shape: CaseShape
30	  turned: boolean // placed turned 90 degrees about up (case W runs along pallet z)
31	  color: vec4 // bright, light-saturated label colour (additive display: no dark colours)
32	}
33	
34	export interface PlannedSlot {
35	  center: vec3 // Pallet-local centre of the case when placed
36	  layer: number // 1..5
37	  turned: boolean // true = turned 90 degrees about up (case W runs along pallet z)
38	  row: number // 0 = far row
39	  col: number // 0 = leftmost case in the row
40	}
41	
42	export const PALLET_SIZE_CM = new vec3(116.5, 15, 116.5)
43	export const PALLET_DECK_Y = 15
44	export const HEIGHT_LIMIT_CM = 180
45	
46	interface OrderLine {key: string, name: string, kg: number, fragile: boolean, layer: number,
47	  w: number, d: number, h: number, count: number, shape: CaseShape, turned: boolean, color: vec4}
48	
49	// The order, sizes W x D x H in cm, already heaviest first. Every case in a layer has the same H,
50	// so each layer finishes level. Layers 3 and 4 are turned so their joints cross the layer below.
51	const ORDER_LINES: OrderLine[] = [
52	  {key: "PetFood", name: "PET FOOD 20kg", kg: 20, fragile: false, layer: 1, w: 55, d: 37, h: 14, count: 6, shape: "sack", turned: false, color: new vec4(1.0, 0.62, 0.5, 1)},
53	  {key: "Laundry", name: "LAUNDRY 4x4L", kg: 17, fragile: false, layer: 2, w: 38, d: 58, h: 30, count: 6, shape: "carton", turned: false, color: new vec4(0.6, 0.55, 1.0, 1)},
54	  {key: "Water", name: "WATER 24", kg: 14, fragile: false, layer: 3, w: 38, d: 58, h: 25, count: 4, shape: "carton", turned: true, color: new vec4(0.35, 0.75, 1.0, 1)},
55	  {key: "Juice", name: "JUICE 12x1L", kg: 12, fragile: false, layer: 3, w: 38, d: 29, h: 25, count: 4, shape: "carton", turned: true, color: new vec4(1.0, 0.7, 0.3, 1)},
56	  {key: "Tomatoes", name: "TINNED TOMATOES 2x24", kg: 10, fragile: false, layer: 4, w: 57, d: 38, h: 13, count: 6, shape: "tray", turned: true, color: new vec4(1.0, 0.42, 0.42, 1)},
57	  {key: "Bread", name: "BREAD", kg: 4, fragile: true, layer: 5, w: 56, d: 45, h: 30, count: 2, shape: "carton", turned: false, color: new vec4(1.0, 0.85, 0.45, 1)},
58	  {key: "PaperTowel", name: "PAPER TOWEL 12", kg: 3, fragile: false, layer: 5, w: 112, d: 25, h: 30, count: 1, shape: "long", turned: false, color: new vec4(0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1)},
59	  {key: "Chips", name: "CHIPS", kg: 2, fragile: true, layer: 5, w: 56, d: 45, h: 30, count: 2, shape: "carton", turned: false, color: new vec4(0.5, 1.0, 0.6, 1)},
60	]
61	
62	// Shown on the pallet when a layer is finished: true for this plan (see the joint check below).
63	const LAYER_DONE_NOTES: {[layer: number]: string} = {
64	  1: "Cartons next: their joints miss the sack seams.",
65	  2: "Next layer turns 90° so the joints cross.",
66	  3: "Flat trays next: keep the top level.",
67	  4: "Light and fragile last: bread, towels, chips.",
68	}
69	
70	function buildOrder(): CaseSpec[] {
71	  const out: CaseSpec[] = []
72	  for (const l of ORDER_LINES) {
73	    for (let k = 0; k < l.count; k++) {
74	      out.push({key: l.key, name: l.name, kg: l.kg, fragile: l.fragile, layer: l.layer,
75	        size: new vec3(l.w, l.h, l.d), shape: l.shape, turned: l.turned, color: l.color})
76	    }
77	  }
78	  return out
79	}
80	
81	export const ORDER: CaseSpec[] = buildOrder()
82	export const LAYER_COUNT = ORDER.reduce((m, c) => Math.max(m, c.layer), 0)
83	
84	/** True when the layer's cases are placed turned 90 degrees (from the order data). */
85	export function isTurnedLayer(layer: number): boolean {
86	  for (const c of ORDER) if (c.layer === layer && c.turned) return true
87	  return false
88	}
89	
90	/** Footprint on the pallet (x = across, z = depth) of a case in the planned orientation. */
91	export function footprint(spec: CaseSpec, turned: boolean): vec2 {
92	  return turned ? new vec2(spec.size.z, spec.size.x) : new vec2(spec.size.x, spec.size.z)
93	}
94	
95	/** Ghost / placed size in pallet axes: the case size with x and z swapped when turned. */
96	export function plannedSize(spec: CaseSpec, turned: boolean): vec3 {
97	  return turned ? new vec3(spec.size.z, spec.size.y, spec.size.x) : spec.size
98	}
99	
100	/**
101	 * Generates the slot plan for the whole order. For each layer: take its cases in order, each with
102	 * its footprint (turned when the line says so), fill a row left to right while it fits the pallet,
103	 * start a new row nearer the user when it doesn't (row depth = deepest case in it), centre each
104	 * row in x and the whole layer in z, and stack the layer on the previous layer's top. Prints an
105	 * error when a layer overflows the pallet or mixes case heights.
106	 */
107	export function buildPlan(order: CaseSpec[]): PlannedSlot[] {
108	  const plan: PlannedSlot[] = []
109	  const S = PALLET_SIZE_CM.x
110	  let bottom = PALLET_DECK_Y
111	  let i = 0
112	  while (i < order.length) {
113	    const layer = order[i].layer
114	    const start = i
115	    while (i < order.length && order[i].layer === layer) i++
116	
117	    const rows: {items: number[], width: number, depth: number}[] = []
118	    for (let k = start; k < i; k++) {
119	      const fp = footprint(order[k], order[k].turned)
120	      let row = rows[rows.length - 1]
121	      if (!row || row.width + fp.x > S + 0.001) {
122	        row = {items: [], width: 0, depth: 0}
123	        rows.push(row)
124	      }
125	      row.items.push(k)
126	      row.width += fp.x
127	      row.depth = Math.max(row.depth, fp.y)
128	    }
129	
130	    const height = order[start].size.y
131	    let depth = 0
132	    for (const r of rows) {
133	      depth += r.depth
134	      if (r.width > S + 0.001) print("[StackRightPickList] ERROR: layer " + layer + " row is " + r.width + " cm wide, pallet is " + S)
135	    }
136	    if (depth > S + 0.001) print("[StackRightPickList] ERROR: layer " + layer + " is " + depth + " cm deep, pallet is " + S)
137	    for (let k = start; k < i; k++) {
138	      if (Math.abs(order[k].size.y - height) > 0.001) {
139	        print("[StackRightPickList] ERROR: layer " + layer + " mixes heights (" + order[k].name + " is " + order[k].size.y + " cm, layer is " + height + " cm)")
140	      }
141	    }
142	
143	    let z = -depth / 2
144	    rows.forEach((r, ri) => {
145	      let x = -r.width / 2
146	      r.items.forEach((k, ci) => {
147	        const fp = footprint(order[k], order[k].turned)
148	        plan.push({
149	          center: new vec3(x + fp.x / 2, bottom + order[k].size.y / 2, z + r.depth / 2),
150	          layer, turned: order[k].turned, row: ri, col: ci,
151	        })
152	        x += fp.x
153	      })
154	      z += r.depth
155	    })
156	    bottom += height
157	  }
158	  return plan
159	}
160	
161	export const PLAN: PlannedSlot[] = buildPlan(ORDER)
162	
163	/** Top of the finished stack above the floor (cm). */
164	export const STACK_HEIGHT_CM = PLAN.reduce((m, s, k) => Math.max(m, s.center.y + ORDER[k].size.y / 2), PALLET_DECK_Y)
165	
166	/** Number of cases in each layer, index = layer. */
167	export function layerCaseCount(layer: number): number {
168	  let n = 0
169	  for (const c of ORDER) if (c.layer === layer) n++
170	  return n
171	}
172	
173	/** True when case i is the last one of its layer in the order. */
174	export function isLastOfLayer(i: number): boolean {
175	  return i < ORDER.length && (i === ORDER.length - 1 || ORDER[i + 1].layer !== ORDER[i].layer)
176	}
177	
178	export function ghostTagText(i: number): string {
179	  return "Layer " + ORDER[i].layer + " · " + (i + 1) + " of " + ORDER.length + " · " + ORDER[i].kg + " kg"
180	}
181	
182	export function layerDoneText(layer: number): string {
183	  return "Layer " + layer + " done.\n" + (LAYER_DONE_NOTES[layer] || "Start the next layer on the ghost.")
184	}
185	
186	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
187	// Plan checks (used by the self-test, the LEAF scenarios and the report)
188	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
189	interface Rect2 {x0: number, x1: number, z0: number, z1: number}
190	
191	function slotRect(k: number): Rect2 {
192	  const fp = footprint(ORDER[k], PLAN[k].turned)
193	  const c = PLAN[k].center
194	  return {x0: c.x - fp.x / 2, x1: c.x + fp.x / 2, z0: c.z - fp.y / 2, z1: c.z + fp.y / 2}
195	}
196	
197	function layerSlots(layer: number): number[] {
198	  const out: number[] = []
199	  for (let k = 0; k < PLAN.length; k++) if (PLAN[k].layer === layer) out.push(k)
200	  return out
201	}
202	
203	/** Pairs of cases in the same layer whose footprints overlap, e.g. "3/4". Empty = no overlaps. */
204	export function planOverlaps(): string[] {
205	  const out: string[] = []
206	  for (let a = 0; a < PLAN.length; a++) {
207	    for (let b = a + 1; b < PLAN.length; b++) {
208	      if (PLAN[a].layer !== PLAN[b].layer) continue
209	      const ra = slotRect(a), rb = slotRect(b)
210	      const ox = Math.min(ra.x1, rb.x1) - Math.max(ra.x0, rb.x0)
211	      const oz = Math.min(ra.z1, rb.z1) - Math.max(ra.z0, rb.z0)
212	      if (ox > 0.01 && oz > 0.01) out.push(a + "/" + b)
213	    }
214	  }
215	  return out
216	}
217	
218	/** Cases whose footprint reaches past the pallet edge. Empty = all inside. */
219	export function planOutsidePallet(): number[] {
220	  const h = PALLET_SIZE_CM.x / 2 + 0.01
221	  const out: number[] = []
222	  for (let k = 0; k < PLAN.length; k++) {
223	    const r = slotRect(k)
224	    if (r.x0 < -h || r.x1 > h || r.z0 < -h || r.z1 > h) out.push(k)
225	  }
226	  return out
227	}
228	
229	/** True when every case in the layer has its top at the same height. */
230	export function isLayerLevel(layer: number): boolean {
231	  const ks = layerSlots(layer)
232	  if (ks.length === 0) return false
233	  const top = PLAN[ks[0]].center.y + ORDER[ks[0]].size.y / 2
234	  for (const k of ks) if (Math.abs(PLAN[k].center.y + ORDER[k].size.y / 2 - top) > 0.01) return false
235	  return true
236	}
237	
238	/** Number of different footprints (size in pallet axes) in the layer. */
239	export function layerFootprintCount(layer: number): number {
240	  const seen: string[] = []
241	  for (const k of layerSlots(layer)) {
242	    const fp = footprint(ORDER[k], PLAN[k].turned)
243	    const key = fp.x.toFixed(1) + "x" + fp.y.toFixed(1)
244	    if (seen.indexOf(key) < 0) seen.push(key)
245	  }
246	  return seen.length
247	}
248	
249	/** A joint: where two neighbouring cases in a layer touch. axis "x" = a line x = at (running along z). */
250	export interface Joint {axis: "x" | "z", at: number, from: number, to: number}
251	
252	export function layerJoints(layer: number): Joint[] {
253	  const ks = layerSlots(layer)
254	  const out: Joint[] = []
255	  for (const a of ks) {
256	    for (const b of ks) {
257	      if (a === b) continue
258	      const ra = slotRect(a), rb = slotRect(b)
259	      if (Math.abs(ra.x1 - rb.x0) < 0.01) {
260	        const from = Math.max(ra.z0, rb.z0), to = Math.min(ra.z1, rb.z1)
261	        if (to - from > 0.01) out.push({axis: "x", at: ra.x1, from, to})
262	      }
263	      if (Math.abs(ra.z1 - rb.z0) < 0.01) {
264	        const from = Math.max(ra.x0, rb.x0), to = Math.min(ra.x1, rb.x1)
265	        if (to - from > 0.01) out.push({axis: "z", at: ra.z1, from, to})
266	      }
267	    }
268	  }
269	  return out
270	}

272	/**
273	 * Joints of `upper` that run along a joint of the layer below (same line within 2 cm, sharing more
274	 * than 5 cm), e.g. "x=0 for 76 cm". Empty = every joint crosses the layer below.
275	 */
276	export function alignedJoints(upper: number): string[] {
277	  const out: string[] = []
278	  const lower = layerJoints(upper - 1)
279	  for (const u of layerJoints(upper)) {
280	    for (const l of lower) {
281	      if (u.axis !== l.axis || Math.abs(u.at - l.at) > 2) continue
282	      const shared = Math.min(u.to, l.to) - Math.max(u.from, l.from)
283	      if (shared > 5) {
284	        const s = u.axis + "=" + (Math.round(u.at * 10) / 10) + " for " + Math.round(shared) + " cm"
285	        if (out.indexOf(s) < 0) out.push(s)
286	      }
287	    }
288	  }
289	  return out
290	}

292	/** One line per layer: rows and footprints, for the log/report. */
293	export function describePlan(): string[] {
294	  const out: string[] = []
295	  for (let l = 1; l <= LAYER_COUNT; l++) {
296	    const rows: string[] = []
297	    for (const k of layerSlots(l)) {
298	      const fp = footprint(ORDER[k], PLAN[k].turned)
299	      const r = PLAN[k].row
300	      rows[r] = (rows[r] ? rows[r] + " + " : "") + ORDER[k].key + " " + fp.x + "x" + fp.y
301	    }
302	    const ks = layerSlots(l)
303	    out.push("layer " + l + (isTurnedLayer(l) ? " (turned)" : "") + ", top " + (PLAN[ks[0]].center.y + ORDER[ks[0]].size.y / 2) +
304	      " cm: " + rows.map((s, r) => "row " + r + " [" + s + "]").join(" | "))
305	  }
306	  return out
307	}

8	export class BoxFactory {

11	  makeMaterial(color: vec4, translucent: boolean): Material {

51	  static layoutWireBox(root: SceneObject, size: vec3, th: number): void {
52	    const hx = size.x / 2, hy = size.y / 2, hz = size.z / 2
53	    const specs: [vec3, vec3][] = []
54	    for (const sy of [-1, 1]) for (const sz of [-1, 1]) specs.push([new vec3(0, sy * hy, sz * hz), new vec3(size.x + th, th, th)])
55	    for (const sx of [-1, 1]) for (const sz of [-1, 1]) specs.push([new vec3(sx * hx, 0, sz * hz), new vec3(th, size.y + th, th)])
56	    for (const sx of [-1, 1]) for (const sy of [-1, 1]) specs.push([new vec3(sx * hx, sy * hy, 0), new vec3(th, th, size.z + th)])

65	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
66	// MeshBuilder shapes for the freight (built once, shared by every case of that shape)
67	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
68	type V3 = [number, number, number]
69	
70	/** Collects triangles and fixes their winding so each one faces `outward` (CCW from outside). */
71	class TriMesh {
72	  verts: number[] = []
73	  idx: number[] = []
74	  private n = 0
75	
76	  vertex(p: V3, nrm: V3): number {
77	    this.verts.push(p[0], p[1], p[2], nrm[0], nrm[1], nrm[2], 0, 0)
78	    return this.n++
79	  }
80	
81	  tri(a: number, b: number, c: number, outward: V3): void {
82	    const P = (k: number): V3 => [this.verts[k * 8], this.verts[k * 8 + 1], this.verts[k * 8 + 2]]
83	    const pa = P(a), pb = P(b), pc = P(c)
84	    const u: V3 = [pb[0] - pa[0], pb[1] - pa[1], pb[2] - pa[2]]
85	    const v: V3 = [pc[0] - pa[0], pc[1] - pa[1], pc[2] - pa[2]]
86	    const cx = u[1] * v[2] - u[2] * v[1], cy = u[2] * v[0] - u[0] * v[2], cz = u[0] * v[1] - u[1] * v[0]
87	    if (cx * outward[0] + cy * outward[1] + cz * outward[2] >= 0) this.idx.push(a, b, c)
88	    else this.idx.push(a, c, b)
89	  }
90	
91	  build(): RenderMesh {
92	    const mb = new MeshBuilder([
93	      {name: "position", components: 3},
94	      {name: "normal", components: 3},
95	      {name: "texture0", components: 2},
96	    ])
97	    mb.topology = MeshTopology.Triangles
98	    mb.indexType = MeshIndexType.UInt16
99	    mb.appendVerticesInterleaved(this.verts)
100	    mb.appendIndices(this.idx)
101	    mb.updateMesh()
102	    return mb.getMesh()
103	  }
104	}
105	
106	function spow(v: number, e: number): number {
107	  return (v < 0 ? -1 : 1) * Math.pow(Math.abs(v), e)
108	}
109	
110	export class ShapeMeshes {
111	  private static pillow: RenderMesh = null
112	  private static tinBodies: RenderMesh = null
113	  private static tinLids: RenderMesh = null
114	
115	  /**
116	   * Soft sack: a 1 cm superellipsoid (boxy in plan, rounded top and bottom), centred on the
117	   * origin. Scale it to the sack size like the 1 cm box mesh.
118	   */
119	  static pillowMesh(): RenderMesh {
120	    if (ShapeMeshes.pillow) return ShapeMeshes.pillow
121	    const m = new TriMesh()
122	    const LAT = 10, LON = 28, eV = 0.55, eH = 0.3
123	    const ring: number[][] = []
124	    for (let i = 0; i <= LAT; i++) {
125	      const th = -Math.PI / 2 + Math.PI * i / LAT
126	      const row: number[] = []
127	      for (let j = 0; j < LON; j++) {
128	        const ph = 2 * Math.PI * j / LON
129	        const r = spow(Math.cos(th), eV)
130	        const p: V3 = [0.5 * r * spow(Math.cos(ph), eH), 0.5 * spow(Math.sin(th), eV), 0.5 * r * spow(Math.sin(ph), eH)]
131	        const len = Math.max(1e-6, Math.sqrt(p[0] * p[0] + p[1] * p[1] + p[2] * p[2]))
132	        row.push(m.vertex(p, [p[0] / len, p[1] / len, p[2] / len]))
133	      }
134	      ring.push(row)
135	    }
136	    const at = (k: number): V3 => [m.verts[k * 8], m.verts[k * 8 + 1], m.verts[k * 8 + 2]]
137	    for (let i = 0; i < LAT; i++) {
138	      for (let j = 0; j < LON; j++) {
139	        const a = ring[i][j], b = ring[i][(j + 1) % LON], c = ring[i + 1][(j + 1) % LON], d = ring[i + 1][j]
140	        const o = at(c), o2 = at(a)
141	        const out: V3 = [o[0] + o2[0], o[1] + o2[1], o[2] + o2[2]]
142	        m.tri(a, b, c, out)
143	        m.tri(a, c, d, out)
144	      }
145	    }
146	    ShapeMeshes.pillow = m.build()
147	    return ShapeMeshes.pillow
148	  }
149	
150	  /**
151	   * Tins for a tray, in cm, centred on the origin in x/z with the tin bottoms at y = 0: a grid of
152	   * `cols` x `rows` short cylinders filling `areaX` x `areaZ`. Bodies and lids are separate meshes
153	   * so they can take different colours. Shared by every tray (all trays in the order are the same).
154	   */
155	  static tinMeshes(cols: number, rows: number, areaX: number, areaZ: number, height: number): RenderMesh[] {
156	    if (ShapeMeshes.tinBodies) return [ShapeMeshes.tinBodies, ShapeMeshes.tinLids]
157	    const SEG = 14
158	    const pitchX = areaX / cols, pitchZ = areaZ / rows
159	    const r = Math.min(pitchX, pitchZ) / 2 - 0.4
160	    const bodies = new TriMesh(), lids = new TriMesh()
161	    for (let cx = 0; cx < cols; cx++) {
162	      for (let cz = 0; cz < rows; cz++) {
163	        const ox = -areaX / 2 + pitchX * (cx + 0.5), oz = -areaZ / 2 + pitchZ * (cz + 0.5)
164	        const bot: number[] = [], top: number[] = [], lid: number[] = []
165	        for (let s = 0; s < SEG; s++) {
166	          const a = 2 * Math.PI * s / SEG
167	          const nx = Math.cos(a), nz = Math.sin(a)
168	          bot.push(bodies.vertex([ox + r * nx, 0, oz + r * nz], [nx, 0, nz]))
169	          top.push(bodies.vertex([ox + r * nx, height, oz + r * nz], [nx, 0, nz]))
170	          lid.push(lids.vertex([ox + (r - 0.3) * nx, height + 0.2, oz + (r - 0.3) * nz], [0, 1, 0]))
171	        }
172	        const centre = lids.vertex([ox, height + 0.2, oz], [0, 1, 0])
173	        for (let s = 0; s < SEG; s++) {
174	          const s2 = (s + 1) % SEG
175	          const am = 2 * Math.PI * (s + 0.5) / SEG
176	          const out: V3 = [Math.cos(am), 0, Math.sin(am)]
177	          bodies.tri(bot[s], bot[s2], top[s2], out)
178	          bodies.tri(bot[s], top[s2], top[s], out)
179	          lids.tri(centre, lid[s], lid[s2], [0, 1, 0])
180	        }
181	      }
182	    }
183	    ShapeMeshes.tinBodies = bodies.build()
184	    ShapeMeshes.tinLids = lids.build()
185	    return [ShapeMeshes.tinBodies, ShapeMeshes.tinLids]
186	  }
187	}

145	   Total 31 cases, deck 15 + 14+30+25+13+30 = 127 cm.
146	   Pick bright, light colours per line (additive display, no dark colours); keep fragile flags for bread and chips.

565	export function palletPoint(c: StackRightController, x: number, y: number, z: number): vec3 {
566	  return c.getPalletWorldTransform().multiplyPoint(new vec3(x, y, z))
567	}
568	
569	/** Grabs case i and drops it a few cm above its slot (inside the 15 cm snap radius). */
570	export function dropOnSlot(c: StackRightController, i: number): void {
571	  c.simulateGrab(i)
572	  c.simulateRelease(i, c.getSlotWorldPosition(i).add(new vec3(0, 5, 0)))
573	}

575	/** Grabs case i and drops it at a Pallet-local point. */
576	export function dropAt(c: StackRightController, i: number, x: number, y: number, z: number): void {
577	  c.simulateGrab(i)
578	  c.simulateRelease(i, palletPoint(c, x, y, z))
579	}

581	/** Waits until no case is sliding (back home or up the queue). */
582	export async function settle(c: StackRightController): Promise<void> {
583	  for (let k = 0; k < 50; k++) {
584	    let busy = false
585	    for (let i = 0; i < c.getCaseCount(); i++) if (c.isCaseReturning(i)) busy = true
586	    if (!busy) return
587	    await sleep(100)
588	  }

594	}

597	export function angleDeg(a: quat, b: quat): number {
598	  const d = Math.min(1, Math.abs(a.w * b.w + a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y + a.z * b.z))
599	  return (2 * Math.acos(d) * 180) / Math.PI

604	  const next = c.getNextIndex()

606	    const inQueue = i >= next && i < next + c.getQueueSize()
607	    if (c.isCaseShown(i) !== (inQueue || c.isCasePlaced(i))) return false

Lens Studio is open with the Stack Right project; devpost/design-brief.md is the approved brief. Work through the CLAD skills and the Lens Studio MCP. Bash and ffmpeg (C:/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg.exe) are available. The learner picks real store orders and says the layers are too perfect: on a real order you often can't finish a layer level, so you build a one-sided step (a hill) and fix it later. Teach exactly that in layer 4. Keep every existing rule, interaction, the ghost/tag/snap/tip/card behaviour, the shapes, the pallet jack, the demo driver and the tests working.
   1. **Order:** insert SOUP 24x500g before the tomato trays: 11 kg, carton, w 38, d 57, h 26, count 3, not fragile, a bright light colour not used yet (light teal or lilac-pink). Layer 4 = 3 soup, then the 6 TINNED TOMATOES 2x24 trays (h 13). Totals: 34 cases, layer 4 top 110 cm, 140 cm with layer 5. Layers 1-3 and 5 unchanged.
   2. **Plan:**
      - Add a per-line zone: "far" = z -58.25 to 0, "near" = z 0 to +58.25 (toward the user), default "full".
      - Soup is far, tomatoes near. Row-pack inside the zone's rectangle: rows centred in x, the zone's rows centred in the zone's z range.
      - When a case doesn't fit the current tier, start a new tier on top of it.
      - Soup: 3 across, 38x57 each, one tier, 26 high. Tomatoes: 38x57 footprints (check the orientation that gives 3 across x 57 deep), 3 per tier, two tiers of 13 = 26.
      - Print an error if a finished layer is not level, a zone overflows, or the step between zones ever exceeds 26 cm during the build.
      - Check layer 4 joints cross layer 3 (joints at x=0 and z=±19, juice at x=±29), and layer 5 crosses layer 4.
      - Tag stays "Layer 4 · K of 34 · kg". Second-tier ghosts sit on top of the first-tier tray. No new mistake rule.
   3. **Step note** when the last soup lands: same style and place as the layer-done note, about 3.5 s or until the next grab. Text: "Not enough soup for a full layer: step at the back." / "The trays fill the front, two high, back to level." Log "[StackRight] step note".
      - Layer 3 done note → e.g. "Layer 3 done.\nHeavy soup next: back half first."
      - Layer 4 done note → "Layer 4 done.\nThe front caught up: level again."
      - Layer 5 unchanged.
   4. **Demo driver:**
      - Keep beats and their [DEMO] lines: intro, case1, overhang, gap, case2, layer1, layer2, layer3mixed, fast, layer5, complete, reset, end.
      - "fast": soup at 1.2 s per case, then "[DEMO] hill" and hold 4 s, then trays at 0.8 s per case, then "[DEMO] level" and hold 1.5 s.
      - "layer5": 2.2 s per case, still hovering 1.5 s over the ghost for the paper towel. Other timings unchanged.
      - Default mode "off" at the end.
   5. **Tests:** update the self-test and LEAF scenarios (Assets/Tests and the copies in devpost/leaf-scenarios) for 34 cases, 140 cm, tags, per-layer notes and the step note. New checks:
      - layer 4 has two zones
      - back is 26 cm higher than front after the soup; the step never exceeds 26 cm
      - second-tier ghosts sit on top of first-tier trays
      - layer 4 is level when finished
      - joints cross for every layer
      - no overlaps within the same zone and tier
      - everything inside the pallet
      Run them and append results to devpost/selftest-2026-11-09.log. Everything must pass.
   6. **Screenshots** (CapturePanelScreenshotTool, Preview, demo camera): (a) step note with the hill in view, (b) mid tray second tier, (c) completion card. Save as devpost/screenshots/v5-*.png. Check the step reads as a step, the note is readable and not hidden, and the card shows 34 cases and 140 cm legibly. Fix what doesn't.
   7. **Re-record** exactly as last time: 30 fps, x264 crf 18, to devpost/video/raw_demo.mp4.
      - First copy the current raw_demo.mp4, demo_beats.log and record_start.txt to *_take5.*.

      - Extract check-hill-note.png (hill + 2 s), check-level.png (level + 0.5 s), and refresh check-completion-card.png; look at each.
      - Set the driver to "off" and save the scene.

Don't touch .agents/skills, .claude/skills or Plugins/. Units are cm; keep everything bright." "Do not git commit, push, or touch anything outside this project folder."
   - **Final report:** what changed per file; the layer 4 plan (zones, tiers, footprints, heights) and whether joints cross for every layer; test totals; recording path/length; demo beat times from recording start; what each check frame shows; anything unfinished or off.

1	// StackRightPickList.ts
2	// STAND-IN FOR BARCODE SCAN. A real picker's Lens would read the case's barcode when it is
3	// picked up. For the preview, the order is fixed: 31 cases of real store freight (sacks, cartons,
4	// shrink-wrapped tin trays, a long carton) in the warehouse system's heaviest-first sequence
5	// (5 layers). The learner should replace these lines with real order lines.
6	//
7	// Owns: the order (case data: name, weight, class, real size in cm, shape, colour, turned flag)
8	// and the LOAD PLAN, which is generated in code from the case sizes (not hand-placed): each layer
9	// is row (shelf) packed - cases in order, left to right while a row fits the 116.5 cm pallet, a
10	// new row nearer the user when it doesn't, row depth = deepest case in it, every row centred in x
11	// and the layer centred in z. Also the plan checks (overlaps, level layers, crossing joints).
12	// Pure data/logic, no scene access.
13	// Must not: touch the scene, hold game state.
14	//
15	// Case sizes are W (x) x H (y) x D (z) in cm, in the case's own frame. Plan positions are in
16	// Pallet-local cm: x right, z toward the user (near edge = +z), y up from the floor.
17	// Pallet deck top is at y = 15.
18	
19	/** How the case is drawn: carton (box), sack (soft bag), tray (tins in a shrink-wrapped tray), long (112 cm carton). */
20	export type CaseShape = "carton" | "sack" | "tray" | "long"
21	
22	export interface CaseSpec {
23	  key: string // used in scene object names, e.g. Case_03_PetFood
24	  name: string // printed on the case
25	  kg: number
26	  fragile: boolean // true = crushable, goes on top
27	  layer: number // 1..5
28	  size: vec3 // W x H x D, cm (case frame)
29	  shape: CaseShape
30	  turned: boolean // placed turned 90 degrees about up (case W runs along pallet z)
31	  color: vec4 // bright, light-saturated label colour (additive display: no dark colours)
32	}
33	
34	export interface PlannedSlot {
35	  center: vec3 // Pallet-local centre of the case when placed
36	  layer: number // 1..5
37	  turned: boolean // true = turned 90 degrees about up (case W runs along pallet z)
38	  row: number // 0 = far row
39	  col: number // 0 = leftmost case in the row
40	}
41	
42	export const PALLET_SIZE_CM = new vec3(116.5, 15, 116.5)
43	export const PALLET_DECK_Y = 15
44	export const HEIGHT_LIMIT_CM = 180
45	
46	interface OrderLine {key: string, name: string, kg: number, fragile: boolean, layer: number,
47	  w: number, d: number, h: number, count: number, shape: CaseShape, turned: boolean, color: vec4}
48	
49	// The order, sizes W x D x H in cm, already heaviest first. Every case in a layer has the same H,
50	// so each layer finishes level. Layers 3 and 4 are turned so their joints cross the layer below.
51	const ORDER_LINES: OrderLine[] = [
52	  {key: "PetFood", name: "PET FOOD 20kg", kg: 20, fragile: false, layer: 1, w: 55, d: 37, h: 14, count: 6, shape: "sack", turned: false, color: new vec4(1.0, 0.62, 0.5, 1)},
53	  {key: "Laundry", name: "LAUNDRY 4x4L", kg: 17, fragile: false, layer: 2, w: 38, d: 58, h: 30, count: 6, shape: "carton", turned: false, color: new vec4(0.6, 0.55, 1.0, 1)},
54	  {key: "Water", name: "WATER 24", kg: 14, fragile: false, layer: 3, w: 38, d: 58, h: 25, count: 4, shape: "carton", turned: true, color: new vec4(0.35, 0.75, 1.0, 1)},
55	  {key: "Juice", name: "JUICE 12x1L", kg: 12, fragile: false, layer: 3, w: 38, d: 29, h: 25, count: 4, shape: "carton", turned: true, color: new vec4(1.0, 0.7, 0.3, 1)},
56	  {key: "Tomatoes", name: "TINNED TOMATOES 2x24", kg: 10, fragile: false, layer: 4, w: 57, d: 38, h: 13, count: 6, shape: "tray", turned: true, color: new vec4(1.0, 0.42, 0.42, 1)},
57	  {key: "Bread", name: "BREAD", kg: 4, fragile: true, layer: 5, w: 56, d: 45, h: 30, count: 2, shape: "carton", turned: false, color: new vec4(1.0, 0.85, 0.45, 1)},
58	  {key: "PaperTowel", name: "PAPER TOWEL 12", kg: 3, fragile: false, layer: 5, w: 112, d: 25, h: 30, count: 1, shape: "long", turned: false, color: new vec4(0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1)},
59	  {key: "Chips", name: "CHIPS", kg: 2, fragile: true, layer: 5, w: 56, d: 45, h: 30, count: 2, shape: "carton", turned: false, color: new vec4(0.5, 1.0, 0.6, 1)},
60	]
61	
62	// Shown on the pallet when a layer is finished: true for this plan (see the joint check below).
63	const LAYER_DONE_NOTES: {[layer: number]: string} = {
64	  1: "Cartons next: their joints miss the sack seams.",
65	  2: "Next layer turns 90° so the joints cross.",
66	  3: "Flat trays next: keep the top level.",
67	  4: "Light and fragile last: bread, towels, chips.",
68	}
69	
70	function buildOrder(): CaseSpec[] {
71	  const out: CaseSpec[] = []
72	  for (const l of ORDER_LINES) {
73	    for (let k = 0; k < l.count; k++) {
74	      out.push({key: l.key, name: l.name, kg: l.kg, fragile: l.fragile, layer: l.layer,
75	        size: new vec3(l.w, l.h, l.d), shape: l.shape, turned: l.turned, color: l.color})
76	    }
77	  }
78	  return out
79	}
80	
81	export const ORDER: CaseSpec[] = buildOrder()
82	export const LAYER_COUNT = ORDER.reduce((m, c) => Math.max(m, c.layer), 0)
83	
84	/** True when the layer's cases are placed turned 90 degrees (from the order data). */
85	export function isTurnedLayer(layer: number): boolean {
86	  for (const c of ORDER) if (c.layer === layer && c.turned) return true
87	  return false
88	}
89	
90	/** Footprint on the pallet (x = across, z = depth) of a case in the planned orientation. */
91	export function footprint(spec: CaseSpec, turned: boolean): vec2 {
92	  return turned ? new vec2(spec.size.z, spec.size.x) : new vec2(spec.size.x, spec.size.z)
93	}
94	
95	/** Ghost / placed size in pallet axes: the case size with x and z swapped when turned. */
96	export function plannedSize(spec: CaseSpec, turned: boolean): vec3 {
97	  return turned ? new vec3(spec.size.z, spec.size.y, spec.size.x) : spec.size
98	}
99	
100	/**
101	 * Generates the slot plan for the whole order. For each layer: take its cases in order, each with
102	 * its footprint (turned when the line says so), fill a row left to right while it fits the pallet,
103	 * start a new row nearer the user when it doesn't (row depth = deepest case in it), centre each
104	 * row in x and the whole layer in z, and stack the layer on the previous layer's top. Prints an
105	 * error when a layer overflows the pallet or mixes case heights.
106	 */
107	export function buildPlan(order: CaseSpec[]): PlannedSlot[] {
108	  const plan: PlannedSlot[] = []
109	  const S = PALLET_SIZE_CM.x
110	  let bottom = PALLET_DECK_Y
111	  let i = 0
112	  while (i < order.length) {
113	    const layer = order[i].layer
114	    const start = i
115	    while (i < order.length && order[i].layer === layer) i++
116	
117	    const rows: {items: number[], width: number, depth: number}[] = []
118	    for (let k = start; k < i; k++) {
119	      const fp = footprint(order[k], order[k].turned)
120	      let row = rows[rows.length - 1]
121	      if (!row || row.width + fp.x > S + 0.001) {
122	        row = {items: [], width: 0, depth: 0}
123	        rows.push(row)
124	      }
125	      row.items.push(k)
126	      row.width += fp.x
127	      row.depth = Math.max(row.depth, fp.y)
128	    }
129	
130	    const height = order[start].size.y
131	    let depth = 0
132	    for (const r of rows) {
133	      depth += r.depth
134	      if (r.width > S + 0.001) print("[StackRightPickList] ERROR: layer " + layer + " row is " + r.width + " cm wide, pallet is " + S)
135	    }
136	    if (depth > S + 0.001) print("[StackRightPickList] ERROR: layer " + layer + " is " + depth + " cm deep, pallet is " + S)
137	    for (let k = start; k < i; k++) {
138	      if (Math.abs(order[k].size.y - height) > 0.001) {
139	        print("[StackRightPickList] ERROR: layer " + layer + " mixes heights (" + order[k].name + " is " + order[k].size.y + " cm, layer is " + height + " cm)")
140	      }
141	    }
142	
143	    let z = -depth / 2
144	    rows.forEach((r, ri) => {
145	      let x = -r.width / 2
146	      r.items.forEach((k, ci) => {
147	        const fp = footprint(order[k], order[k].turned)
148	        plan.push({
149	          center: new vec3(x + fp.x / 2, bottom + order[k].size.y / 2, z + r.depth / 2),
150	          layer, turned: order[k].turned, row: ri, col: ci,
151	        })
152	        x += fp.x
153	      })
154	      z += r.depth
155	    })
156	    bottom += height
157	  }
158	  return plan
159	}
160	
161	export const PLAN: PlannedSlot[] = buildPlan(ORDER)
162	
163	/** Top of the finished stack above the floor (cm). */
164	export const STACK_HEIGHT_CM = PLAN.reduce((m, s, k) => Math.max(m, s.center.y + ORDER[k].size.y / 2), PALLET_DECK_Y)
165	
166	/** Number of cases in each layer, index = layer. */
167	export function layerCaseCount(layer: number): number {
168	  let n = 0
169	  for (const c of ORDER) if (c.layer === layer) n++
170	  return n
171	}
172	
173	/** True when case i is the last one of its layer in the order. */
174	export function isLastOfLayer(i: number): boolean {
175	  return i < ORDER.length && (i === ORDER.length - 1 || ORDER[i + 1].layer !== ORDER[i].layer)
176	}
177	
178	export function ghostTagText(i: number): string {
179	  return "Layer " + ORDER[i].layer + " · " + (i + 1) + " of " + ORDER.length + " · " + ORDER[i].kg + " kg"
180	}
181	
182	export function layerDoneText(layer: number): string {
183	  return "Layer " + layer + " done.\n" + (LAYER_DONE_NOTES[layer] || "Start the next layer on the ghost.")
184	}
185	
186	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
187	// Plan checks (used by the self-test, the LEAF scenarios and the report)
188	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
189	interface Rect2 {x0: number, x1: number, z0: number, z1: number}
190	
191	function slotRect(k: number): Rect2 {
192	  const fp = footprint(ORDER[k], PLAN[k].turned)
193	  const c = PLAN[k].center
194	  return {x0: c.x - fp.x / 2, x1: c.x + fp.x / 2, z0: c.z - fp.y / 2, z1: c.z + fp.y / 2}
195	}
196	
197	function layerSlots(layer: number): number[] {
198	  const out: number[] = []
199	  for (let k = 0; k < PLAN.length; k++) if (PLAN[k].layer === layer) out.push(k)
200	  return out
201	}
202	
203	/** Pairs of cases in the same layer whose footprints overlap, e.g. "3/4". Empty = no overlaps. */
204	export function planOverlaps(): string[] {
205	  const out: string[] = []
206	  for (let a = 0; a < PLAN.length; a++) {
207	    for (let b = a + 1; b < PLAN.length; b++) {
208	      if (PLAN[a].layer !== PLAN[b].layer) continue
209	      const ra = slotRect(a), rb = slotRect(b)
210	      const ox = Math.min(ra.x1, rb.x1) - Math.max(ra.x0, rb.x0)
211	      const oz = Math.min(ra.z1, rb.z1) - Math.max(ra.z0, rb.z0)
212	      if (ox > 0.01 && oz > 0.01) out.push(a + "/" + b)
213	    }
214	  }
215	  return out
216	}
217	
218	/** Cases whose footprint reaches past the pallet edge. Empty = all inside. */
219	export function planOutsidePallet(): number[] {
220	  const h = PALLET_SIZE_CM.x / 2 + 0.01
221	  const out: number[] = []
222	  for (let k = 0; k < PLAN.length; k++) {
223	    const r = slotRect(k)
224	    if (r.x0 < -h || r.x1 > h || r.z0 < -h || r.z1 > h) out.push(k)
225	  }
226	  return out
227	}
228	
229	/** True when every case in the layer has its top at the same height. */
230	export function isLayerLevel(layer: number): boolean {
231	  const ks = layerSlots(layer)
232	  if (ks.length === 0) return false
233	  const top = PLAN[ks[0]].center.y + ORDER[ks[0]].size.y / 2
234	  for (const k of ks) if (Math.abs(PLAN[k].center.y + ORDER[k].size.y / 2 - top) > 0.01) return false
235	  return true
236	}
237	
238	/** Number of different footprints (size in pallet axes) in the layer. */
239	export function layerFootprintCount(layer: number): number {
240	  const seen: string[] = []
241	  for (const k of layerSlots(layer)) {
242	    const fp = footprint(ORDER[k], PLAN[k].turned)
243	    const key = fp.x.toFixed(1) + "x" + fp.y.toFixed(1)
244	    if (seen.indexOf(key) < 0) seen.push(key)
245	  }
246	  return seen.length
247	}
248	
249	/** A joint: where two neighbouring cases in a layer touch. axis "x" = a line x = at (running along z). */
250	export interface Joint {axis: "x" | "z", at: number, from: number, to: number}
251	
252	export function layerJoints(layer: number): Joint[] {
253	  const ks = layerSlots(layer)
254	  const out: Joint[] = []
255	  for (const a of ks) {
256	    for (const b of ks) {
257	      if (a === b) continue
258	      const ra = slotRect(a), rb = slotRect(b)
259	      if (Math.abs(ra.x1 - rb.x0) < 0.01) {
260	        const from = Math.max(ra.z0, rb.z0), to = Math.min(ra.z1, rb.z1)
261	        if (to - from > 0.01) out.push({axis: "x", at: ra.x1, from, to})
262	      }
263	      if (Math.abs(ra.z1 - rb.z0) < 0.01) {
264	        const from = Math.max(ra.x0, rb.x0), to = Math.min(ra.x1, rb.x1)
265	        if (to - from > 0.01) out.push({axis: "z", at: ra.z1, from, to})
266	      }
267	    }
268	  }
269	  return out
270	}
271	
272	/**
273	 * Joints of `upper` that run along a joint of the layer below (same line within 2 cm, sharing more
274	 * than 5 cm), e.g. "x=0 for 76 cm". Empty = every joint crosses the layer below.
275	 */
276	export function alignedJoints(upper: number): string[] {
277	  const out: string[] = []
278	  const lower = layerJoints(upper - 1)
279	  for (const u of layerJoints(upper)) {
280	    for (const l of lower) {
281	      if (u.axis !== l.axis || Math.abs(u.at - l.at) > 2) continue
282	      const shared = Math.min(u.to, l.to) - Math.max(u.from, l.from)
283	      if (shared > 5) {
284	        const s = u.axis + "=" + (Math.round(u.at * 10) / 10) + " for " + Math.round(shared) + " cm"
285	        if (out.indexOf(s) < 0) out.push(s)
286	      }
287	    }
288	  }
289	  return out
290	}
291	
292	/** One line per layer: rows and footprints, for the log/report. */
293	export function describePlan(): string[] {
294	  const out: string[] = []
295	  for (let l = 1; l <= LAYER_COUNT; l++) {
296	    const rows: string[] = []
297	    for (const k of layerSlots(l)) {
298	      const fp = footprint(ORDER[k], PLAN[k].turned)
299	      const r = PLAN[k].row
300	      rows[r] = (rows[r] ? rows[r] + " + " : "") + ORDER[k].key + " " + fp.x + "x" + fp.y
301	    }
302	    const ks = layerSlots(l)
303	    out.push("layer " + l + (isTurnedLayer(l) ? " (turned)" : "") + ", top " + (PLAN[ks[0]].center.y + ORDER[ks[0]].size.y / 2) +
304	      " cm: " + rows.map((s, r) => "row " + r + " [" + s + "]").join(" | "))
305	  }
306	  return out
307	}

import sys, os
d = sys.argv[1]


def edit(name, pairs):
    p = os.path.join(d, name)
    s = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
    for a, b in pairs:

   - **(1) Order:** insert SOUP 24x500g (11 kg, carton, w38 d57 h26, count 3, not fragile, bright unused colour) before the tomato trays. Layer 4 = 3 soup, then 6 tray cases (h13). Totals: 34 cases, layer 4 top 110 cm, 140 cm overall.
   - **(2) Plan:**
     - Zones: far z -58.25..0, near 0..+58.25, default full. Soup far, tomatoes near.
     - Row-pack within the zone; when a case doesn't fit, start a new tier on top.
     - Print an error when a finished layer isn't level, a zone overflows, or the step exceeds 26 cm.
     - Joints must cross for every layer. The tag stays "Layer 4 · K of 34 · kg". Second-tier ghosts sit on the first-tier tray. No new mistake rule.
   - **(3) Notes:**
     - Step note when the last soup lands: same style and place as the layer note, about 3.5 s or until the next grab. Text: "Not enough soup for a full layer: step at the back." / "The trays fill the front, two high, back to level." Log "[StackRight] step note".
     - Layer 3 note: "Layer 3 done.\nHeavy soup next: back half first."
     - Layer 4 note: "Layer 4 done.\nThe front caught up: level again."
   - **(4) Demo:**
     - Keep the beats: intro, case1, overhang, gap, case2, layer1, layer2, layer3mixed, fast, layer5, complete, reset, end.
     - "fast": soup 1.2 s/case, "[DEMO] hill" + hold 4 s, trays 0.8 s/case, "[DEMO] level" + hold 1.5 s.

   - Joints use the bottom face of the upper layer against the top face of the lower layer, with a 1.5 cm touching tolerance (the zones are centred in their halves, so there is a 1.25 cm gap at z = 0).

#!/bin/sh
# usage: record.sh <scratch dir>; records the Preview region until "[DEMO] end" appears in the LS log after start.

OFF=$(stat -c %s "$L"); echo "$OFF" > "$S/log_offset.txt"; rm -f "$S/stop.flag"
date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%3N" > $V/record_start.txt
{ while [ ! -f "$S/stop.flag" ]; do sleep 0.1; done; printf q; sleep 6; } | \
  /c/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg.exe -y -f gdigrab -framerate 30 -offset_x 2292 -offset_y 87 -video_size 1476x830 -draw_mouse 0 -i desktop -c:v libx264 -preset veryfast -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p $V/raw_demo.mp4 > "$S/ffmpeg.log" 2>&1 &

done
date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%3N" > "$S/stop_time.txt"; touch "$S/stop.flag"; wait

commands.name: analyze-drive
commands.description: Drive the VRC-local analyze sub-agents (C20 Perfetto root-cause, C22 synthesis, C19 architecture pass) as an LLM. Use when analyzing a Perfetto trace for a perf violation, synthesizing findings, or running a source-grounded architecture pass on an app. (user)

commands.name: attack
commands.description: Run the whole hackathon machine for one event from this chat. Use for /attack <slug>, or when the user asks to attack, enter or continue a hackathon through hackathon_archetype. (user)

commands.name: da-scout
commands.description: Replay a developer-recorded TapeDeck VRS deterministically, collect Quest performance and app-health evidence, and inspect the replay journal. Use as the replay leaf of an external VRC tape-route run. Do not use it to drive or record gameplay. (user)

commands.name: domain-modeling
commands.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model. (user)

commands.name: grilling
commands.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases. (user)

commands.name: handoff
commands.description: Write a short handoff file so work can continue after /clear or compaction with no lost context. Use when the user says handoff, wrap up this session, save progress, or is about to /clear, or when a context-watch reminder asks for one. (user)

commands.name: hz-android-2d-porting
commands.description: Guides porting existing Android 2D apps to Meta VR and Horizon OS — input adaptation, panel layout, and design requirements. Use when adapting a mobile Android app for Meta VR. For UI design decisions, use hz-panel-designer if available. Build path: Standard Android; use hz-quest-verify-first if the build path is unclear. (user)

commands.name: hz-api-upgrade
commands.description: Upgrades Meta VR apps to newer Horizon OS SDK versions — migration guides, deprecated API replacements, changelog. Use when updating SDK versions or fixing deprecated API warnings. Build paths: all Meta VR app stacks; use hz-quest-verify-first if the build path is unclear. (user)

commands.name: hz-immersive-designer
commands.description: Guides design of comfortable, intuitive VR/MR experiences for Meta VR and Horizon OS — comfort guidelines, interaction patterns, spatial layout, accessibility. Use during UX design review or when evaluating comfort and accessibility. Build paths: Meta Spatial SDK, Unity, Unreal, native OpenXR, and WebXR; for 2D panel apps use hz-panel-designer if available. Use hz-quest-verify-first if the build path is unclear. (user)

commands.name: hz-iwsdk-webxr
commands.description: Builds WebXR experiences for Meta VR and Horizon OS using the Immersive Web SDK (IWSDK) — ECS architecture, Three.js integration, spatial UI. Use when creating web-based VR/MR apps for Quest Browser. (user)

commands.name: hz-metavrx-layout-sdk
commands.description: Build multi-window Meta Horizon OS experiences with the MetaVrx Layout SDK in Jetpack Compose or React Native. Covers framework selection, setup, anchoring, semantic offsets, window promotion, fallback, priority, lifecycle, and theming. Use for apps that need multiple app-owned panels without an immersive scene. Build path: Standard Android, including React Native; use hz-quest-verify-first if the path is unclear, and do not use this skill for immersive Spatial SDK scenes. (user)

commands.name: hz-metavrx-ui-set
commands.description: Builds app UI for Meta VR and Horizon OS with the MetaVrx UI Set, a Jetpack Compose component library and design system. Covers UiSetTheme, buttons, cards, controls, dialogs, dropdowns, inputs, side navigation, sliders, tooltips, the Icons.Regular library, Gradle setup, and migration from the Spatial SDK UI Set. Build path: Standard Android; use hz-quest-verify-first if the path is unclear. (user)

commands.name: hz-new-project-creation
commands.description: Scaffolds new Meta VR and Horizon OS projects after the build path is selected — Standard Android, Meta Spatial SDK, Unity, Unreal, or WebXR. Use when creating a new Meta VR app from scratch. Build paths: all; use hz-quest-verify-first to choose the path. (user)

commands.name: hz-perfetto-debug
commands.description: Analyzes Meta VR and Horizon OS VR performance using Perfetto traces — frame timing, CPU/GPU bottlenecks, render pass analysis. Use when profiling frame drops, jank, or thermal issues on Meta VR devices. Build paths: all Meta VR app stacks; use hz-quest-verify-first if the build path is unclear. (user)

commands.name: hz-platform-sdk
commands.description: Guides integration of the Horizon Platform SDK for Meta VR and Horizon OS Android/Kotlin apps — achievements, IAP, users, leaderboards, presence, notifications, abuse reporting, entitlements, asset files, application lifecycle, consent, device integrity, language packs, user age categories, and rate and review. Covers setup, initialization, API usage, data types, error handling, and best practices for all 17 public platform SDK packages. Build paths: Standard Android and Meta Spatial SDK; use hz-psdk-integration for guided integration, hz-unity-platform-sdk for Unity/C#, and hz-quest-verify-first if the path is unclear. (user)

commands.name: hz-psdk-integration
commands.description: Guides interactive Horizon Platform SDK (PSDK) integration for Meta VR and Horizon OS Android/Kotlin apps — analyzes the codebase, recommends public platform features, plans the integration, and validates on device. Use for workflow guidance; use hz-platform-sdk for the detailed API reference. Build paths: Standard Android and Meta Spatial SDK; use hz-quest-verify-first if the path is unclear. (user)

commands.name: hz-quest-verify-first
commands.description: MANDATORY pre-flight check before answering any question or writing any code related to Meta Quest VR headsets (Quest 2, Quest 3, Quest 3S, Quest Pro) or apps that target them. Forces verification against authoritative Meta sources via the metavr CLI / metavr MCP tools BEFORE relying on training-data knowledge. Counters the failure mode where agents answer Quest-related questions from stale memory and ship deprecated APIs, broken Android manifests, and store-rejected builds. Loads automatically when the user is in a Quest project (any reference to Oculus / Meta Quest / Horizon OS, Unity OVR or Meta XR packages, com.meta.* / com.oculus.* package IDs, Quest-targeted AndroidManifest, .meta files, or developers.meta.com / developer.oculus.com URLs). Build paths: all; use this skill first whenever the path is unknown or a Quest-specific claim is involved. (user)

commands.name: hz-react-native-expo

Use when the user wants to build or run a Meta VR app in React Native/Expo, load a JS bundle URL on a headset, set up expo-horizon-core, or get live reload on device. commands.name: meta-vr:metavr-cli

commands.name: ls-clad:build-mesh
commands.description: (ls-clad) Generate a 3D mesh, model, or asset for a Lens — build, create, or make props, characters, scenery. GLB backends return the file plus AABB metadata so the caller can size colliders and place the mesh in the world.

commands.name: ls-clad:build-music
commands.description: (ls-clad) Generate musical phrases, chord progressions, beats, jingles, and short pieces via local algorithmic synthesis. Sample-free, license-clean, fully offline. commands.argumentHint: description of the musical piece to generate (genre, mood, tempo, length)

commands.name: ls-clad:build-sfx
commands.description: (ls-clad) Generate non-pitched sound effects (UI, impacts, sweeps, foley, ambient textures, retro 8-bit) via local algorithmic synthesis. Outputs 44.1 kHz WAV to Assets/GeneratedSFX/. For musical phrases or chord progressions use /build-music instead.
commands.argumentHint: description of the sound effect to generate

commands.name: ls-clad:camera-and-rendering

commands.name: ls-clad:lens-js-debugger
commands.description: (ls-clad) Debug a running JS Lens. Use when you need to evaluate expressions, set breakpoints, pause/resume execution, or inspect runtime state in a Lens Studio preview or on a Specs device.

commands.name: ls-clad:lens-log-analysis
commands.description: (ls-clad) Lens Studio log format, severity prefixes, and how to interpret RunAndCollectLogsTool's inline result fields. Use when analyzing logs, debugging compilation failures, or reading preview runtime output.

commands.name: ls-clad:lens-package-toolkit
commands.description: (ls-clad) Lens Studio native packages: install from Asset Library, pack/unpack `.lsc`/`.lspkg`, bump versions, attach README/`.d.ts`, author setup scripts. APIs `NativePackageDescriptor`, `exportScript`/`exportPackage`, `unpack`, `instantiate`, `SetupScript`.

commands.name: ls-clad:lens-studio-field-notes
commands.description: (ls-clad) Plugin-specific field notes for Lens Studio work — scene/asset tool selection (VirtualScene-first), the domain-skill index, Editor API delegation specifics, and scene-prep slash commands. Loaded by /lens-studio-router.

commands.name: ls-clad:lens-studio-router
commands.description: (ls-clad) Front door for any Lens Studio / Specs / Spectacles / Snapchat Lens task — invoke PROACTIVELY at the start of such a conversation, before the user names a skill. ('specs'/'Spectacles' = Snap's AR glasses, not test specs/RSpec; 'snapchat' = a Lens in the camera, not a 3rd-party API.) Gates LS 5.22+ / project / MCP readiness (never scaffolds; if cwd isn't an LS project, asks you to open it and restart the session so MCP is picked up), uses the platform you named (asks Specs vs Snapchat only if you didn't), then routes to the platform workflow.

commands.name: ls-clad:materials
commands.description: (ls-clad) Material creation, configuration, and assignment patterns for Lens Studio scene construction. commands.name: ls-clad:mesh-builder-scripting

commands.name: ls-clad:perfetto-trace-analysis
commands.description: (ls-clad) Analyzes Perfetto (.pftrace) traces for Lens Studio—quick JSON summary first, then optional deep SQL via a persistent trace server. Use when the user mentions .pftrace, Perfetto, Mobile Lens Profiler, Spectacles Monitor traces, frame drops, jank, LAT, or trace performance analysis.

commands.name: ls-clad:physics

Use when wiring `BodyComponent`/`ColliderComponent`/`ConstraintComponent`/`WorldComponent`, building ragdolls, vehicles, breakables, or draggable props, debugging tunneling/constraints, or using `Physics.ForceMode`/`createGlobalProbe`/`addPointConstraint`/`WorldSettingsAsset`/`Matter`/`Filter`. Fires on `.esproj` with `Physics.*` or code like `body.addForce`/`probe.rayCast`. commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: artifact-capabilities
commands.description: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.

commands.name: update-config

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify

Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: code-review

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

  - New SOUP 24x500g line: 11 kg carton, 38×57×26 cm, 3 cases, back half (far zone).
  - Tomatoes go in the front half (near zone).
  - The plan fills each zone row by row and starts a second tier on top when the next case doesn't fit. It prints an error if a finished layer isn't level, a zone overflows, or the step goes over 26 cm.

- [StackRightController.ts](Desktop/specs_hackathon/pallet_lens/Assets/Scripts/StackRightController.ts): the step note shows when the last soup lands, in the same style and place as the layer note. It stays 3.5 s or until the next grab and logs `[StackRight] step note`.

  - New still mode `hill`; `layer4` now holds a tray over its second-tier ghost.
  - The `fast` beat runs soup 1.2 s/case, `[DEMO] hill` + 4 s, trays 0.8 s/case, then `[DEMO] level` + 1.5 s.
  - `layer5` runs at 2.2 s/case.
  - Self-test updated for 34 cases.

- **Back half:** 3 soup cases, one tier, top at 110 cm.
- **Front half:** 3 trays on 3 trays, two tiers of 13 cm, also reaching 110 cm.

| 2 | x=±19, z=0 |
| 3 | x=0, z=±19, x=±29 |

[raw_demo.mp4](Desktop/specs_hackathon/pallet_lens/devpost/video/raw_demo.mp4) is 101.7 s at 30 fps, x264 crf 18. - [check-hill-note.png](Desktop/specs_hackathon/pallet_lens/devpost/video/check-hill-note.png): pink soup standing at the back, the front half still at layer 3 height, both lines of the step note readable, tag "Layer 4 · 23 / 34".
